title.narrative: Sri Lankan workforce have more and better employment opportunities

description.narrative:
"Sri Lanka faces high unemployment driven by economic crises, climate shocks, and vulnerabilities in micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), focusing on challenges such as skills gaps, informality, and barriers faced by women, youth, and persons with disabilities in accessing decent work.
ILO's technical assistance addresses low productivity, poor working conditions, limited access to finance, and climate vulnerabilities, supporting MSMEs’ resilience and fostering entrepreneurship in green sectors such as renewables and waste management. ILO also promotes policies for a just transition to a green economy, ensuring that workers in carbon intensive industries and informal sectors receive reskilling and social protections to mitigate displacement risks. Partnerships with government agencies, private investors, NGOs, and trade unions facilitate community level adaptation, sustainable enterprise development, and inclusive green job creation. The strategy is led by the Ministry of Labour in collaboration with employers’ organizations, trade unions and the financial institutions which provides technical support through EIIP. It prioritizes rural workers including farmers and fishers, crisis affected MSMEs, marginalized groups, and green entrepreneurs seeking sustainable job transitions. "
